page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.large is a burstable instance type belonging to the ecs.t6 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 2 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it operates on the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.t6-c1m4.large delivers entry-level performance. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance scored 1161.28 and multi-core scored 2371.48, both falling into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests showed 187.49 GB/sec for cached small blocks, but dropped to 22.38 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, which is categorized in the bottom 10%. PassMark CPU and memory scores also align with the bottom 25% and bottom 10% tiers respectively, reflecting limited processing and memory throughput under sustained loads.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its burstable CPU allocation and low baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps. While it supports advanced CPU instructions such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography, its actual execution speeds are constrained, as seen in the PassMark encryption test scoring 969.78, which is in the bottom 10%. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this hardware profile is designed for low-cost, low-utilization scenarios where continuous high performance is not required, allowing users to leverage CPU credits for occasional spikes.

Given these performance characteristics, the ecs.t6-c1m4.large is best suited for lightweight workloads. Appropriate use cases include low-traffic static web serving, basic development or testing environments, simple background tasks, and microservices that do not require sustained CPU or high network throughput. It is not recommended for database operations, large-scale data processing, or real-time LLM inference due to its poor performance in these categories.
